what_it_does: Modern AI systems use many GPUs working together, but those GPUs are not all connected equally — some share very fast internal links while others talk across slower external links. When many GPUs flood those slower links, traffic jams form and performance drops sharply. NetCrafter addresses this by applying three tricks at the boundary between fast and slow parts of the network: it packs small half-filled data packets together so less space is wasted (flit stitching), it cancels packets that were sent speculatively but are not yet needed (flit trimming), and it lets the most time-sensitive packets jump ahead of bulk traffic in line (flit sequencing). Together these ideas squeeze more useful work out of the slower links without touching the GPU's internal compute logic, which is a relatively low-risk change to an otherwise complex system.
